span.label: the degradation problem - IDENTIFIED BY TRAINING ERROR, NOT TEST ERROR: accuracy saturates then degrades rapidly with depth, and the authors' point is that this is NOT overfitting because adding layers raises the TRAINING error - the distinction is what makes it an optimisation problem rather than a generalisation one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: an identity mapping - AN IDEALISATION THE PAPER WITHDRAWS: the argument for residual learning runs through the case where identity mappings are optimal and the solver can drive the weights to zero, and the authors then state in their own words that in real cases this is unlikely
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the residual mapping - A REFORMULATION, PRESENTED AS A HYPOTHESIS: instead of fitting the desired underlying mapping the layers fit its residual, and the claim that this is easier to optimise is given in the authors' own words as something they hypothesize
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
